requirements.requirement: New user passwords on node1 must be at least 12 characters long
requirements.summary: libpam-pwquality installed and wired into /etc/pam.d/common-password ahead of pam_unix; pwquality.conf set minlen=12. Self-service password change with a shorter password (8-9 chars) was directly rejected with 'password is shorter than 12 characters' both before (cmd-fd1d94daad9d429f) and after a full reboot (cmd-3d25a26e26a94291), and a compliant 14-char password was accepted (cmd-a11b60314b1343f9).

requirements.requirement: New user passwords on node1 must use at least three different character classes
requirements.summary: pwquality.conf set minclass=3. Self-service change to a 14-char, all-lowercase-plus-digit password (2 classes) was directly rejected with 'password contains less than 3 character classes' (cmd-aa2eba635bce4151); the same compliant password with upper/lower/digit/symbol (4 classes) was accepted (cmd-a11b60314b1343f9). Config persisted after reboot (cmd-5816a2de9b7a44f6).

requirements.requirement: Policy must persist across a restart (bonus/expected robustness given mandatory restart evidence protocol)
requirements.summary: Boot identity changed from 2dffe735-... to cebf3731-... across a reboot (cmd-c6b2c629647540e6, cmd-1b2f6f4cdc30470c, cmd-a76d00fda4de40b3), confirmed by the fixed lifecycle snapshots (global:before_prepare:node1:boot-identity vs global:after_executor:node1:boot-identity). PAM stack ordering and pwquality.conf settings were re-verified intact post-reboot (cmd-5816a2de9b7a44f6), and live enforcement was re-validated with a fresh test user rejecting a too-short password (cmd-3d25a26e26a94291).

overall_summary: Both material requirements -- minimum 12-character length and at least 3 character classes for new/self-service user passwords on node1 -- are directly demonstrated as enforced via libpam-pwquality/pwquality.conf, with rejection and acceptance tests both before and after a full node reboot proving persistence. Test users were fully cleaned up and no residue or failed services remain. The task was completed cleanly with no unnecessary mutations.
limitations: Root-set passwords (via `passwd <user>` as root) bypass pwquality enforcement per standard PAM/Linux behavior (visible in cmd-20038d2db7f3407e, cmd-1e46aecd6dd74be8, cmd-cd6e830a38764ea7); only self-service passwd changes were shown to be enforced. This is expected root-override behavior, not a policy gap, but was not explicitly called out as intentional by the executor.

Verification relied on two ephemeral test users created and deleted by the executor rather than inspection of any pre-existing account; this is a reasonable and low-risk approach but means no real end-user password change was observed.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands map cleanly to the task: installing libpam-pwquality (cmd-464d75eff0d64ed2, cmd-a8468357854e4759) was necessary to implement the policy; editing pwquality.conf (cmd-a77812fe996a4a42) implemented it; creating test users pwtestuser and pwtestuser2 and exercising passwd changes (cmd-e08628608a8f4ba6, cmd-20038d2db7f3407e, cmd-1e46aecd6dd74be8, cmd-fd1d94daad9d429f, cmd-aa2eba635bce4151, cmd-a11b60314b1343f9, cmd-cd6e830a38764ea7, cmd-3d25a26e26a94291) were bounded verification steps, and both test users were fully deleted afterward (cmd-d8f8d2d8dbe446d6, cmd-1b2590bc946c4b95), leaving no residue -- confirmed by after_executor temporary-files and failed-services snapshots showing no leftover artifacts beyond expected boot-specific systemd-private directories. The reboot (cmd-2641e970a1e7472e) was for the mandatory restart-evidence protocol, not the task contract, but was bounded and fully recovered with no failed services or package-health issues in after_executor snapshots. No unnecessary or unreverted mutations identified.
